headline: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva tells countries to act faster on debt and AI rules.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept; speech of 7 Oct read in full on two wire copies, no overstatement.
importance_line: The IMF's call for faster action on debt and AI rules affects governments and their citizens first, and it is a speech warning ahead of the Bangkok meetings rather than a new policy.
summary: The Associated Press reports that Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund, said in a speech in Singapore on Wednesday, 7 Oct 2026, that rich and poor countries must act faster to cut debt while the AI boom, heavy borrowing and wars strain their economies. She warned that if AI company earnings fall short, heavy borrowing by the biggest cloud computing companies and large global holdings of US stocks could turn a disappointment into a far-reaching shock.
notes: Read on AP wire copy (Bozeman Daily Chronicle) and TBS copy; AP page itself blocked (403). Speech date 7 Oct 2026 (Wednesday). Named person positioned: IMF managing director. Source chain: AP is the first reporter.
